hero.filename: USS Yorktown (CV-10) underway during the Marianas operation, in June 1944 (80-G-238298).jpg
hero.title: File:USS Yorktown (CV-10) underway during the Marianas operation, in June 1944 (80-G-238298).jpg
hero.source: USS Yorktown (CV-10) underway during the Marianas operation, in June 1944 (80-G-238298)
hero.description:
The U.S. Navy aircraft carrier USS Yorktown (CV-10) underway during the Marianas operation, in June 1944. The ship is painted in Camouflage Measure 33, Design 10A. Aircraft of Carrier Air Group 1 (CVG-1) are spotted on the flight deck: 16 Grumman F6F Hellcat fighters, five Grumman TBF Avenger torpedo bombers, and seven Curtiss SB2C Helldiver dive bombers.
The photograph was received by the U.S. Naval Photographic Science Laboratory on 17 July 1944.
categories: Images from the Naval History and Heritage Command

gallery.title: File:S-2E landing on USS Yorktown 1969.jpg
gallery.artist: Journalist Seaman Samuel Goldstein, U.S. Navy
gallery.credit: U.S. Navy photo [1] U.S. Navy website [2]
gallery.description: A U.S. Navy Grumman S-2E Tracker (BuNo 153566) of anti-submarine squadron VS-27 Pelicans, assigned to Carrier Anti-Submarine Air Group 56 (CVSG-56), after landing on the aircraft carrier USS Yorktown (CVS-10) in the North Atlantic in November 1969. gallery.artist: Lt. Charles E. Kerlee, U.S. Navy
gallery.credit: U.S. Navy photo 80-G-K-14833; Scan from Robert L. Lawson (ed.): The History of US Naval Air Power. The Military Press, New York (USA), 1985. ISBN 0-517-414813, p. 85.
gallery.source: F6F-3 Hellcats aboard USS Yorktown (CV-10), 31 August 1943 (80-G-K-14833)
gallery.description: The U.S. Navy aircraft carrier USS Yorktown (CV-10) during the Marcus Island raid on 31 August 1943: Lt. Comdr. James H. "Jimmy" Flatley,Commander of Air Group 5 (CAG-5), sits in his Grumman F6F-3 Hellcat (code "00"), painted in a tricolor-scheme (certainly an "in the field" application) before takeoff. An Aviation Boatswain Mate stands ready to remove chock from wheels. A non-specular insignia white diagonal stripe on the tail and the green propeller hub signified CAG-5 aboard the Yorktown.

gallery.description: The U.S. Navy aircraft carrier USS Yorktown (CV-10) underway, circa in mid-1943, possibly during her shakedown cruise in the late spring. Planes on deck include Grumman F6F-3 Hellcat fighters and Curtiss SB2C-1 Helldiver dive bombers. Note this carrier's unique longitudinal black flight deck stripe and the absence of any hull numbers on the flight deck.

gallery.filename: Murderers row at Ulithi Atoll - US Third fleet carriers at anchor on 8 December 1944 (80-G-294131).jpg
gallery.title: File:Murderers row at Ulithi Atoll - US Third fleet carriers at anchor on 8 December 1944 (80-G-294131).jpg
gallery.artist: photographed from a USS Ticonderoga (CV-14) plane.
gallery.description: U.S. Third Fleet aircraft carriers at anchor in Ulithi Atoll, 8 December 1944, during a break from operations in the Philippines area. The carriers are (from front to back): USS Wasp (CV-18), USS Yorktown (CV-10), USS Hornet (CV-12), USS Hancock (CV-19) and USS Ticonderoga (CV-14). Wasp, Yorktown and Ticonderoga are all painted in camouflage Measure 33, Design 10a. The other Essex-class carrier painted in sea blue Measure 21 is USS Lexington (CV-16).
categories: Images from the Naval History and Heritage Command

gallery.filename: Fantail of USS Mobile (CL-63), October 1943.jpg
gallery.title: File:Fantail of USS Mobile (CL-63), October 1943.jpg
gallery.artist: Photographed by Photographer's Mate Alphonso Ianelli.
gallery.description: View on the fantail of the U.S. Navy light cruiser USS Mobile (CL-63), looking across her open aircraft hangar hatch toward the starboard quarter, during the October 1943 raid on Marcus Island. Vought OS2U-3 Kingfisher floatplanes are on her catapults. The plane on the starboard catapult has a small bomb under its wing. USS Yorktown (CV-10) is in the center distance.

gallery.filename: Curtiss SB2C-1 Helldivers of VB-1 return to USS Yorktown (CV-10), in July 1944 (80-G-241043).jpg
gallery.title: File:Curtiss SB2C-1 Helldivers of VB-1 return to USS Yorktown (CV-10), in July 1944 (80-G-241043).jpg
gallery.artist: Photographer's Mate First Class O.L. Smith, USNR.
gallery.description:
U.S. Navy Curtiss SB2C-1 Helldiver bombers of Bombing Squadron 1 (VB-1) return to the aircraft carrier USS Yorktown (CV-10) after a raid in early July 1944.
Note: The original caption for this photograph, released by Commander in Chief, Pacific, gives the date as 6 July 1944 and identifies the target as Chichi Jima, Bonin Islands, which was actually attacked on 4 June. Edward Steichen's "U.S. Navy War Photographs" identifies the target as Guam.

gallery.filename: Task Force 77 in South China Sea, 1965.jpg
gallery.title: File:Task Force 77 in South China Sea, 1965.jpg
gallery.description: The U.S. Navy Task Force 77 operating in the South China Sea, March 1965. It had recently launched strikes against North Vietnam. Carriers present are (clockwise from bottom): Ranger (CVA-61), Yorktown (CVS-10), Coral Sea (CVA-43) and Hancock (CVA-19). The guided missile cruiser Canberra (CAG-2) is in the center of the formation. The destroyer screen includes: England (DLG-22), Gurke (DD-783), Rogers (DD-876), Walker (DD-517), O'Bannon (DD-450), Somers (DD-947), Jenkins (DD-447), John A. Bole (DD-755), Higbee (DD-806), Buck (DD-761), Joseph Strauss (DDG-16) and Ernest G. Small (DD-838).This photograph was specially posed, and does not represent a normal operating formation.

gallery.filename: USS Pictor (AF-54) replenishing USS Yorktown (CVA-10) and USS Bausell (DD-845) in 1957.jpg
gallery.title: File:USS Pictor (AF-54) replenishing USS Yorktown (CVA-10) and USS Bausell (DD-845) in 1957.jpg
gallery.description: The U.S. Navy stored ship USS Pictor (AF-54) replenishing the aircraft carrier USS Yorktown (CVA-10) and the destroyer USS Bausell (DD-845), in 1957. Yorktown, with assigned Carrier Air Group 19 (CVG-19), was deployed to the Western Pacific from 9 March to 25 August 1957. Following this cruise, Yorktown was redesignated as an anti-submarine carrier ("CVS") on 1 September 1957.

gallery.filename: US Navy Task Group 58.1 underway in July 1944.jpg
gallery.title: File:US Navy Task Group 58.1 underway in July 1944.jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Navy (photographed with a K-17 camera from a USS Hornet (CV-12) plane)
gallery.description: The U.S. Navy Task Force 58 raids in the Caroline Islands, July 1944: Rear Admiral J.J. Clark's Task Group 58.1 reverses course, during attacks on Yap, 28 July 1944. The aircraft carrier USS Hornet (CV-12) is in the center, with the light carrier USS Cabot (CVL-28) in the left middle distance and USS Yorktown (CV-10) at right. Six Grumman F6F Hellcat fighters are overhead.

gallery.filename: US Navy Task Force 50 underway to the Gilbert Islands in November 1943.jpg
gallery.title: File:US Navy Task Force 50 underway to the Gilbert Islands in November 1943.jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Navy (photographed from a USS Lexington (CV-16) Douglas SBD-5 Dauntless)
gallery.description: U.S. Navy ships of Task Force 50 at sea, en route to the Gilbert and Marshall Islands on 23 November 1943, the day that USS Lexington (CV-16) fighters shot down 17 Japanese planes flying from the Marshalls. The aircraft carrier USS Lexington (CV-16) is in the center, turning into the wind to recover planes. USS Cowpens (CVL-25) is at left, the battleship USS South Dakota (BB-57) in center distance, and USS Yorktown (CV-10) and USS Washington (BB-56) are at right.
